content: 1. The name of the company must be provided. 2. The national or local authority company license number must be included. 3. The address of the company should be detailed, including the city, province/territory/state, country, postal code, mailing address, telephone or cellular number (with area code and extension), email address, and optionally, a fax number. 4. If the company operates from multiple physical locations, a separate list must be attached. This list should include the address of each location, the name and license number of the pest control operator (PCO) in charge, and the validity period of their license. 5. Vehicle information must be provided, including the vehicle registration number. Additionally, it must be stated whether the vehicle has a separate and well-ventilated cabin for storing chemicals, equipment, and contaminated clothing. 6. The name of the company owner or manager must be specified. 7. The pest control activities performed by the company should be indicated, such as general pest control (excluding fumigation, Category A) or fumigation (Category B). 8. The names, license numbers, and license categories of all licensed pest control operators employed by the company must be provided. If necessary, a separate list should be attached. 9. The position of the applicant must be stated, and the company stamp and date must be included. Application Form for Pest Control Operator License 1. The applicant's first name, middle initial, and last name must be provided. 2. The date and place of birth, as well as citizenship, must be included. 3. Educational qualifications must be documented, with a certified copy of the certificate attached. 4. PCO certification must be provided, with a copy of the certificate attached if relevant. 5. Details of work experience in pest control activities must be included. 6. The applicant's address, including city, province/territory/state, country, postal code, mailing address, telephone or cellular number (with area code and extension), email address, and optionally, a fax number, must be provided. 7. The category of license applied for must be indicated: general pest control (excluding fumigation, Category A) or fumigation (Category B). 8. The following supporting documents must be attached: Two recent passport-sized photographs (5x5 cm), one of which must be countersigned as a true likeness. A certified copy of the educational qualification certificate. A certified copy of a document proving citizenship. The applicable fee. 9. The applicant must declare that the information provided is accurate and complete to the best of their knowledge and acknowledge the penalties for providing false information. The declaration must be signed, dated, and include the applicant's printed name. Pest Control Operation Report 1. The date the pest management activity was carried out must be recorded. 2. The address of the premises where the activity was conducted must be provided. 3. The type of premises (e.g., factory, office, silo, ship hold, or residence) must be specified. 4. The name and contact details (telephone number or other contact information) of the owner, occupier, or person requesting the activity must be included. 5. The purpose of the pest management activity must be stated, including a description of the pest situation (type, density) and justification for the chosen control option. 6. Details of the pesticide(s) used must be provided, including the active ingredient, trade name/registration number, batch number, method of application, concentration of the diluted solution, rate of application, and total amount of diluted solution used. 7. The start and finish times of the pest control operation must be recorded. 8. The vehicle registration number must be included. 9. The client must be advised on the pest management activity, including precautions to be taken and the re-entry period. This must be acknowledged by ticking the applicable box. 10. Any additional comments should be noted. 11. The PCO and, if applicable, the Assistant PCO (APCO) must sign the report, including their names, license numbers, and the date. 12. The client must acknowledge receipt of the report by signing and dating it. Certification Course for Pest Control Operators (Category A) 1. The course should cover pesticide laws and regulations of the country. 2. General information about pesticides, including their importance, formulations, selection of appropriate chemical control strategies, and safe handling and use, must be included. 3. Symptoms of pesticide poisoning, first aid, and decontamination procedures must be taught. 4. Integrated pest or vector management should be covered. 5. The biology and ecology of major pests, their public health and economic importance, and their identification must be included. 6. The use of pesticide application equipment in the public health sector and effective, quality-assured pesticide applications must be addressed. 7. Personal protective equipment (PPE) must be discussed. 8. Re-entry intervals after pesticide application must be explained. 9. Instructions on how to read and use Safety Data Sheets (SDS) must be provided. 10. Operational procedures, preparation of spray materials, and precautions must be taught. 11. Proper handling of pesticides, including disposal of unwanted pesticides and containers, as well as spill prevention and management, must be included. 12. Management of vectors, pests of public health importance, stored product pests, and structural pests such as termites must be covered, including their life cycles, susceptible stages, and habitat identification. 13. Record-keeping of operations must be emphasized. 14. Familiarity with the Code of Conduct and access to technical and national guidelines related to pest control operators must be ensured. 15. Provisions for those wishing to perform fumigation activities must include special training and examination on fumigation. Certification Course for Assistant Pest Control Operators 1. General information about pesticides, including formulations, selection of appropriate chemical control strategies, and safe handling and use, must be included. 2. The use of pesticide application equipment in the public health sector must be taught. 3. Operational procedures, preparation of spray materials, and precautions for quality and effective pesticide application must be covered. 4. The biology and ecology of major pests, their public health and economic importance, and their identification must be included. 5. Personal protective equipment (PPE) must be discussed. 6. Re-entry intervals after pesticide application must be explained. 7. Instructions on how to read and use Safety Data Sheets (SDS) must be provided. 8. Proper handling of pesticides, including disposal of unwanted pesticides and containers, must be included. 9. Record-keeping of operations must be emphasized. 10. Familiarity with national guidelines on pest control operators and accessing them must be ensured. Certification Course for Fumigation (Category B) 1. The course should cover different types of fumigation, including space fumigation and soil fumigation. 2. Common fumigants, including their properties, formulations, uses, applications, precautionary measures, personal protective equipment, and disposal, must be discussed. 3. The advantages and disadvantages of fumigation must be explained. 4. Factors affecting the effectiveness of fumigation must be addressed.
